name: AppHeader
description: The top bar of an application: a slot for a sidebar toggle, the breadcrumbs, a search button that opens your command palette, your own actions, a notifications bell with an unread count and the account menu. In a narrow space the search folds to an icon.

leading.description: Content at the very start, such as the button that opens or folds the sidebar. Give it an accessible name.

breadcrumbs.description: Where the person is, usually Breadcrumbs. It takes the free space and shortens before anything else.

onSearch.description: Shows the search button and calls this when it is pressed, e.g. to open a CommandPalette. The shortcut shown on it is a hint only: wire the key yourself.

searchLabel.description: Text and accessible name of the search button.

searchShortcut.description: The shortcut hint on the search button, keys separated by a space. Shown only where there is room. Pass an empty string to hide it.

onNotifications.description: Shows the notifications bell and calls this when it is pressed, e.g. to open a panel.

notificationCount.description: How many notifications are unread. Drawn as a badge (99+ above 99) and read with the button's name. Zero or none draws no badge.

notificationsLabel.description: Accessible name of the bell. The count is added: "Notifications, 3 unread".

actions.description: Your own buttons, before the bell and the account menu.

userMenu.description: The account menu at the end, normally a UserMenu.

permissions.description: What the person may do: { search, notifications } as "allow" (default), "disabled" or "hidden", or { state, reason }. A disabled button stays focusable (aria-disabled) and says why. The server must check again.

label.description: Accessible name of the header landmark.

size.description: default is 56 px high; compact is 44 px with smaller controls.

border.description: Draw a line under the header.

sticky.description: Keep the header at the top while the page scrolls.

classNames.description: Class names for the parts, by slot name, added after the built-in ones. Slots: root, leading, breadcrumbs, search, shortcut, actions, notifications, badge, user-menu.

keyboard: Tab: moves through the leading control, the breadcrumbs, search, your actions, the bell and the account menu, in that order
Enter or Space: presses a button
requirements: The bar is a header landmark with its own name; use one per page and keep the page's main landmark outside it
The search button has a visible name, or an accessible name when it folds to an icon; the shortcut hint is for sighted keyboard users and is hidden from screen readers so the name is not read twice
The bell is named with the unread count ("Notifications, 3 unread"); the badge is drawn as a number, not as color alone
A disabled button stays focusable (aria-disabled) and its reason is read with it
The breadcrumbs keep their own navigation landmark

use_when: The bar across the top of an application page, inside or beside a sidebar
You want search, notifications and the account menu in one consistent place on every page
avoid_when: You need the whole frame with the sidebar and the phone menu: use DashboardShell
Navigation across the top of a marketing site: use TopNav
A title and the actions for one page: use PageHeader below the bar
anti_patterns: A second search field in the page next to the search button: one search entry point
A count badge with no number for screen readers: set notificationCount instead of drawing your own dot
More than two or three buttons in the actions slot: move the rest into a menu
UI permission is not security: hiding or disabling a button only changes what people see, so the server must check again for every request

contract.data: A notification count and the slots you fill: breadcrumbs, actions and the account menu.
customization: leading, breadcrumbs, actions and userMenu slots
